summary: Electric hydrofoiling vessels for passenger, hospitality, and tourism routes.
editor_note: Short marine routes get a purpose-built electric vessel: Vessev designs, builds, and assembles hydrofoils in-house, while the VS-9 pairs an 8.95 m hull with quiet, low-wake passenger operation. Compared to electrifying a conventional ferry, lifting above the water attacks drag and ride quality together. The coherent vessel-and-route bet earns the feature; certification, charging, and fleet utilization will determine the economics.

product_evidence.claim: Vessev designs, builds, and assembles its electric hydrofoiling vessels in-house for passenger, hospitality, waterfront, and tourism routes.
The VS-9 is an 8.95 m by 3.1 m electric hydrofoil intended to reduce wake, noise, energy use, and ride motion on commercial routes.

market_context.primary_user: Ferry, hospitality, tourism, and waterfront operators serving short coastal routes.
market_context.differentiation: Hydrofoiling reduces hydrodynamic drag and wake while the company controls vessel design and assembly in-house.
market_context.why_now: Battery improvements and waterfront decarbonization create room for smaller electric vessels on routes poorly served by conventional ferries.

risks.claim: Commercial economics depend on certification, charging access, maintenance, and consistently high vessel utilization.
risks.basis: The company is moving from a first certified vessel toward multi-market fleet deployments.
